what_happened: A job that adds a producer build-slot step was paused at the $10 budget while still in planning. The plan review had found a gap: a global-flag case the plan missed. The paused job could not be corrected and no retry would run. The the person running Athena re-queued the work by hand and wrote the plan review's finding (the global-flag gap) into the new request. No job id is attached to the event.
cause: A paused job is a dead end. Athena offers no way to correct a job that stopped at its budget cap, and none to resume it or re-queue it with a fresh budget. The findings from planning rounds live only in that job's records, so they do not carry into a new job. The the person running Athena has to pick the finding out and restate it as detailed instructions, which is the the person running Athena doing Athena's work. The $10 spend in planning also shows that nothing compares planning cost with the cap while planning is running.
prevention: Add an Athena command that follows a budget-paused job. It creates a successor job with a fresh budget. It copies the accepted reading and the last critic findings (blocker and major ones) into the successor's reading automatically. It links the successor to the paused job and closes the old one with a clear record. It also warns, before the cap is reached, when planning spend nears the cap. The the person running Athena then runs one command, with no hand-written diagnosis, and the intervention is logged.
proposed_request: When a job pauses at its budget cap during planning, Athena must offer one command to continue it without the the person running Athena rewriting anything. The command makes a successor job with a new budget. The successor's reading carries over the paused job's accepted reading and the plan review's unresolved blocker and major findings, such as the global-flag gap in the producer build-slot step. The paused job is closed and linked to the successor. A warning is also shown when planning spend passes 80% of the cap. Acceptance: (1) a test pauses a job at the cap in planning and checks that the command makes a successor holding the earlier findings; (2) the paused job is recorded as closed with a link to the successor; (3) a test checks that the warning appears at 80% of the cap; (4) the command works on a job that has no findings.
